evidence.note: Started supervisor and ran happy-path HTTP tests (auth, workspaces, messages), read logs — found and fixed a store.py bug (65), showing verification driving fixes.

Tested IRC gateway, verified bidirectional bridging by reading IRC-posted message back through the API, and tested WebSocket subscribe + cross-node fanout — direct invariant checks across HTTP/WS/IRC.
Actively simulated both required failure scenarios: killed the broadcast relay to test resilience, and SIGKILLed HTTP node 0 to verify the other nodes keep serving — the core adversarial probes.
Tested replay/resume across different nodes and verified dense per-channel seq with the relay dead — the seq-density-under-partition invariant the grader checks.
Drove the SPA with Playwright/chromium, iterated on UI failures across many restart+retest cycles, and verified the pinned data-testid selectors were present in served HTML and JS.
Broad error/behavior coverage: file upload limits, search, exact /shrug bytes, roles/permissions 403s, invite-only restrictions, empty-channel state — confirming status codes and edge semantics.

reasoning: The agent built targeted checks spanning all four transports, verified dense per-channel seq under mixed writers and cross-node replay, drove the SPA against pinned testids, and — critically — actively killed both an HTTP node and the broadcast relay to confirm continued writes and seq density, fully satisfying the level-8 anchor and reaching most of level-10's specifics (browser pass, edited/deleted semantics, cross-node fanout, failures driving fixes with re-verification). It falls short of a clean 10 because verification was a series of ad-hoc bash scripts rather than a single repeatable harness and I saw no explicit node-restart-within-60s re-check, placing it at 9.
